title: Countable cohomology criterion for a perfect telescope
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Perfect means etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. A space is quasi-compact if its point space is quasi-compact and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$ such that $\mathcal O_X(V)$ is countable for every affine scheme $V$ etale over $X$. Let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ have $\mathcal H^i(K)(V)$ countable for every integer $i$ and every such $V$. There exist a sequence of perfect objects $P_m$ of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ with transition maps $t_m:P_m\to P_{m+1}$ and maps $a_m:P_m\to K$ with $a_{m+1}t_m=a_m$ such that $K$, with these legs, is a homotopy colimit: the coproduct map $(a_m)_m$ fits into a distinguished triangle $\bigoplus_mP_m\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\bigoplus_mP_m\to K\to(\bigoplus_mP_m)[1]$. All sums are small ambient derived sums. Homotopy colimit has the meaning of [def-kun-truncations].

source.place: Tag 0CRV, lemma-countable, implication (2) to (1); legs are the derived-colimit convention of derived.tex Tags 090Z and 0CRH. The perfect objects lie in D_QCoh: the proof produces them through the equivalence D_QCoh(O_X) = D(A,d) of theorem-DQCoh-is-Ddga.

proof.text: Choose a perfect compact generator $G$ of $C_X=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ by [lem-sfb-space-compact-perfect-generator]. Its shifted Hom groups detect zero objects, exactly as required by [lem-sfb-space-generator-dg-equivalence]. Apply that node to obtain $(A,d)$ and the exact equivalence $F:C_X\simeq D(A,d)$ with quasi-inverse $T$. For every integer $i$ it gives $H^i(A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G,G[i])$ and $H^i(F(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G,K[i])$.

source.place: Tag 0CRV, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1), choice of generator and DG model; Tag 09MC, theorem-DQCoh-is-Ddga.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-countable-perfect-ext] with $E=G$. The hypotheses are precisely the given countability of affine etale structure rings and of all cohomology sheaves of $K$; $G$ is perfect by step 1. Thus both Hom groups in step 1 are countable. Hence $H^i(A)$ and $H^i(M)$ are countable for every integer $i$, where $M=F(K)$. Apply [lem-sfb-dg-countable-compact-telescope] to get compact $Q_m$, transitions $u_m$, legs $b_m:Q_m\to M$, and their telescope triangle with third object $M$.

source.place: Tag 0CRV, lemma-countable, final paragraph using Tag 0CRU, lemma-countable-cohomology, and dga.tex Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable.

proof.text: An equivalence preserves every existing coproduct: the bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(T(\bigoplus N_j),L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\bigoplus N_j,F(L))\cong\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}(N_j,F(L))\cong\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}(T(N_j),L)$ give its universal property, with the specified coprojections. The same applies to $F$. These bijections and the defining bijection for compactness show that $P_m=T(Q_m)$ is compact in $C_X$. By [lem-sfb-space-compact-objects-perfect] each $P_m$ is perfect. The coproducts in $C_X$ are the ambient derived coproducts by [lem-sfb-space-perfect-localizing-generation].

source.place: Tag 0CRV, lemma-countable, transport through the equivalence; Tag 09M8, proposition-compact-is-perfect; equivalence universal-property calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-functor-preserves-hocolim] to the exact, coproduct-preserving $T$ and the triangle of step 2. Let $\epsilon:TF\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{C_X}$ be its counit. Set $t_m=T(u_m)$ and $a_m=\epsilon_K T(b_m)$; then $a_{m+1}t_m=\epsilon_K T(b_{m+1}u_m)=a_m$. The image triangle, using the coproduct comparison $\bigoplus T(Q_m)\simeq T(\bigoplus Q_m)$ and $\epsilon_K$, has first arrow $1-\mathrm{shift}$ and second arrow restricting to $a_m$ on each coprojection. It is therefore the required distinguished triangle with third object $K$, by [def-kun-truncations]. Its ambient interpretation follows from step 3.

lean.statement: theorem exists_perfect_telescope_of_countable {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.SmallModules] (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : X.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated) (hO : ∀ V : X.EtaleSite, IsAffine (X.etaleForget.obj V) → Countable (X.structureSheaf.obj.obj (op V))) (K : X.DerivedQCoh) (hK : ∀ (i : ℤ) (V : X.EtaleSite), IsAffine (X.etaleForget.obj V) → Countable (((X.smallModuleEquivalence.inverse).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.SmallModules i).obj K.obj)).val.obj (op V))) : ∃ (P : ℕ → X.DerivedQCoh) (t : ∀ m : ℕ, (P m).obj ⟶ (P (m + 1)).obj) (a : ∀ m : ℕ, (P m).obj ⟶ K.obj) (B : X.DerivedModules) (ι : ∀ m : ℕ, (P m).obj ⟶ B) (hc : IsColimit (Cofan.mk B ι)) (q : K.obj ⟶ B⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧), (∀ m : ℕ, SheafOfModules.IsPerfectOnRingedSiteOfUniverses.{u, u, 0, w} X.smallStructureSheaf (P m).obj) ∧ (∀ m : ℕ, t m ≫ a (m + 1) = a m) ∧ Triangle.mk (𝟙 B - (@id (B ⟶ B) (hc.desc (Cofan.mk B (fun m : ℕ ↦ t m ≫ ι (m + 1)))))) (hc.desc (Cofan.mk K.obj a)) q ∈ distTriang X.DerivedModules
